title: Weekly Dose of Optimism #218
gist: Packy McCormick's weekly optimism roundup: the FDA gave accelerated approval to INOVIO's Voceryq, the first US plasmid DNA immunotherapy (7 of 26 RRP patients surgery-free for a year; stock tripled with cash due to run out Q1 2027), and Zipline raised $1.5B at a $21.5B valuation to scale drone delivery to 300 Walmart supercenters. It also covers the first human DREADD study (~93% seizure reduction in 3 epilepsy patients), DARPA NOM4D's first automated in-space assembly demo, and UVA's 2,500+ documented reincarnation cases.

insights.claim: The FDA granted accelerated approval to INOVIO's Voceryq, the first plasmid DNA-based immunotherapy approved in the US, for recurrent respiratory papillomatosis (RRP) caused by HPV types 6 and 11.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: A new therapeutic modality has cleared US regulators, de-risking plasmid DNA immunotherapy as a category.
insights.quote: the FDA granted accelerated approval to INOVIO’s Voceryq, the first plasmid DNA-based immunotherapy approved in the US.
insights.locator: (1) FDA Approves Voceryq, the First Plasmid DNA Immunotherapy

insights.claim: Voceryq delivers two plasmids into muscle cells — one encoding HPV-6/HPV-11 proteins to train the immune system against infected cells and one encoding IL-12 to amplify the immune response — using electrical pulses (electroporation) instead of a viral vector.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Non-viral DNA delivery avoids viral-vector constraints and is the core of INOVIO's platform claim.
insights.quote: A device fires brief electrical pulses that open temporary pores in cell membranes so the DNA can get inside without requiring a virus for delivery.
insights.locator: (1) FDA Approves Voceryq, the First Plasmid DNA Immunotherapy

insights.claim: In Voceryq's small open-label trial, 7 of 26 adults who had each needed at least three surgeries in the prior year required no surgery for the full following year; results still must be confirmed in a follow-up study.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Efficacy evidence is thin (n=26, open-label); confirmatory study is a key risk for the accelerated approval.
insights.quote: After treatment, 7 of the 26 patients in the trial didn’t need surgery for the entire following year.
insights.locator: (1) FDA Approves Voceryq, the First Plasmid DNA Immunotherapy

insights.claim: INOVIO was set to run out of cash in Q1 2027 before the approval, and its stock tripled in after-hours trading after posting the results — the approval was effectively the company's last shot.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Binary-outcome biotech: approval rescued a near-insolvent company, illustrating extreme event risk in single-asset small caps.
insights.quote: The company was set to run out of cash in Q1 2027, but its stock tripled in after hours after posting the results.
insights.locator: (1) FDA Approves Voceryq, the First Plasmid DNA Immunotherapy

insights.claim: RRP patients have gone from no non-surgical treatment to two — Precigen's virus-based Papzimeos (full approval August 2025) and INOVIO's Voceryq — creating direct competition in a small indication.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Voceryq enters a market with an already fully-approved competitor, limiting its commercial upside in RRP alone.
insights.quote: Precigen’s Papzimeos, which uses a modified virus to target the same HPV types, won full approval in August 2025.
insights.locator: (1) FDA Approves Voceryq, the First Plasmid DNA Immunotherapy

insights.claim: The plasmid platform is likely more important than the RRP indication: swapping in different instructions could target other HPV diseases, cancers and infections, which INOVIO plans to pursue next.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Value of INOVIO hinges on platform extensibility beyond RRP rather than the first approved product.
insights.quote: the platform will likely prove to be even more important.
insights.locator: (1) FDA Approves Voceryq, the First Plasmid DNA Immunotherapy

insights.claim: Zipline raised $1.5 billion at a $21.5 billion valuation in a round led by Paradigm, WCM and Layer, to bring drone delivery nationwide in the US.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Large late-stage capital is flowing into autonomous drone logistics at a premium valuation.
insights.quote: The company raised $1.5 billion at a $21.5 billion valuation in a round led by Paradigm, WCM, and Layer.
insights.locator: (2) Zipline Raises $1.5B to Build Nationwide Drone Network

insights.claim: Zipline CEO Keller Clifton said flight volumes grew 18x over the past 18 months and the company now does more than a million deliveries per year per metro.
insights.speaker: Keller Clifton
insights.so_what: Rapid volume scaling suggests drone delivery has moved past pilot stage in US metros.
insights.quote: they’ve grown flight volumes 18x and are now doing more that a million deliveries per year per metro.
insights.locator: (2) Zipline Raises $1.5B to Build Nationwide Drone Network

insights.claim: Zipline signed what it calls the largest autonomous vehicle contract in history with Walmart to scale automated delivery to 300 Walmart supercenters across the US.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Walmart's commitment gives drone delivery national retail distribution and is a competitive signal for last-mile logistics.
insights.quote: with whom they’ll scale to 300 supercenters throughout these United States.
insights.locator: (2) Zipline Raises $1.5B to Build Nationwide Drone Network

insights.claim: Zipline reports over 150 million commercial autonomous miles with no safety incidents, with drones that are quiet, fast, affordable and need no human chaperone.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: A clean safety record is the key regulatory and public-acceptance moat for scaling drones nationwide.
insights.quote: they’ve done over 150M commercial autonomous miles with no safety incidents
insights.locator: (2) Zipline Raises $1.5B to Build Nationwide Drone Network

insights.claim: McCormick is highly optimistic that a large share of physical movement will shift to the skies, framing Zipline's expansion as a major step in that direction.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Author sees aerial logistics as a structural theme, not a niche.
insights.quote: I’m incredibly optimistic that a good deal of movement will move to the skies
insights.locator: (2) Zipline Raises $1.5B to Build Nationwide Drone Network

themes.theme: DREADDs as a new control knob in humans

insights.claim: DREADDs are engineered receptors delivered by viral vector to chosen cells; they stay inert until activated by CNO, a drug that binds only to them, giving on-demand control with apparently no off-target effects.
insights.speaker: Owl Posting
insights.so_what: Designer receptor plus exclusive ligand creates a genuinely new, orthogonal therapeutic control mechanism.
insights.quote: Then you administer CNO, which binds exclusively to the DREADDs.
insights.locator: (3) DREADDs Work in Humans

insights.claim: In the first adult human DREADD study, inhibitory DREADDs placed in the hippocampus of 3 people with medication-resistant epilepsy cut seizures by about 93% with only mild side effects.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Tiny n=3 but striking effect size: chemogenetics may open a path for precise, dialable treatment of brain circuit disorders.
insights.quote: cutting seizures by ~93% with only mild side effects.
insights.locator: (3) DREADDs Work in Humans

insights.claim: Today large space structures are either folded and deployed (like the James Webb Space Telescope) or assembled by hand from pieces launched over many missions (like the ISS); DARPA's NOM4D pursues a third option of launching a box of parts and assembling them autonomously.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Automated assembly could remove rocket-fairing size limits on orbital infrastructure.
insights.quote: They can send up a box of parts and assemble them in an automated way.
insights.locator: (4) NOM4D Program Demonstrates Automated In-Space Assembly

insights.claim: DARPA announced that a Caltech payload completed what it calls the first-ever demonstration of automated in-space assembly: a simple three-axis gantry robot joined composite truss pieces while unrolling a reflective mesh, as a proof of concept for space antennas.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Milestone shows low-complexity robotics can build structures in orbit, a prerequisite for large antennas and solar arrays.
insights.quote: DARPA announced that a Caltech payload had done just that, in what the agency calls the first-ever demonstration of automated in-space assembly.
insights.locator: (4) NOM4D Program Demonstrates Automated In-Space Assembly

insights.claim: NOM4D targets structures from hundreds of meters to kilometers across — space depots, habitats, huge solar arrays and very large radio antennas — using deliberately simple, Tinkertoy-like components rather than advanced robotics.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Signals defense-backed demand for kilometer-scale orbital infrastructure over the long term.
insights.quote: NOM4D is aiming at structures hundreds of meters to kilometers across, like space depots, habitats, huge solar arrays, and radio antennas
insights.locator: (4) NOM4D Program Demonstrates Automated In-Space Assembly

insights.claim: Varda Space Industries, a Not Boring Capital portfolio company, is manufacturing drugs in orbit aboard its W-7 mission, targeting crystallization of PROTAC molecules that are hard to crystallize on Earth.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: In-space pharma manufacturing is operating, though author has a portfolio conflict.
insights.quote: We are making drugs in space aboard W-7 as we tweet.
insights.locator: (4) NOM4D Program Demonstrates Automated In-Space Assembly

insights.claim: Since psychiatrist Ian Stevenson founded the Division of Perceptual Studies at the University of Virginia in the 1960s, researchers there have documented and coded more than 2,500 cases of young children spontaneously reporting detailed past-life memories.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Author frames reincarnation as better-researched than assumed; evidential value is contested.
insights.quote: researchers there have documented and coded more than 2,500 cases worldwide of young children who spontaneously report detailed memories of previous lives.
insights.locator: (5) Telepathy Tapes Season 3: The Reincarnation Records

insights.claim: McCormick argues reincarnation is a compelling bridge to believing the world is more magical than we appreciate, and urges balancing technological 'Means' stories with 'Meaning'.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Reflects the author's broader worldview pairing tech optimism with openness to the paranormal.
insights.quote: Reincarnation is a compelling bridge to believing that the world is more magical than we appreciate.
insights.locator: (5) Telepathy Tapes Season 3: The Reincarnation Records

insights.claim: Sponsor Runway says 65M+ people use its platform to generate, edit and produce video, images and audio with 80+ media models, and that 95%+ of the Fortune 100 are among its users, accessible also via an MCP inside ChatGPT, Claude, Grok, Cursor and Replit.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Promotional claims, but indicate generative video is reaching enterprise scale and distribution via agent tool protocols.
insights.quote: 65M+ people use Runway to generate, edit and produce video, images and audio with 80+ top media models.
